newsitem.title: UK: CU French acquisitions earnings enhancing.
newsitem.headline: CU French acquisitions earnings enhancing.

text.p: British composite insurer Commercial Union upped its share of the French life market to around 4.5 percent on Thursday.

The company has bought 73.1 percent of SEV ("Societe d'Epargne Viagere"), a French life assurer, and 100 percent of a French insurance broking business, which distributes products of life insurance organisation AFER ("Association Francaise d'Epargne et de Retraite") products, from Compagnie de Suez.
Commercial Union already owned 1.9 percent of SEV.
The company's finance director Peter Foster said it had been very pleased when the stake was offered to them by Suez.
The move splits the overall group's business split between life and general insurance to 50:50 based on 1996 pro forma numbers for 1996.
The deal, said Foster would be earnings enhancing in its first yaer, met the company's return on capital objectives and cemented the arrangements with AFER.

At the time of the acquisition of Groupe Victoire by Commercial Union in 1994, AFER, Compagnie de Suez and Commercial Union agreed on a structure whereby Abeille vie, the life assurance subsidiary of Commercial Union France, and SEV, would take equal shares of future AFER new business production.
With more than 500,000 members and approximately 13 billion stg of assets under management, AFER is the largest association of savers in France.
The net assets acquired, including the embedded value of the existing business, were worth about 90 million stg as of December 31 1996.
The acquisition, which is subject to approvals by the French and European authorities, will be financed from Commercial Union France's existing resources.
